scams.name: The Jinetero Friendship Hustle
scams.avoidance: It's fine to chat and explore, but know that most jineteros work on commission Research restaurants and bars in advance on Cuba travel forums Walk away from 'guides' who seem to steer rather than accompany
scams.location: Old Havana (La Habana Vieja), especially near the Malecón

scams.name: 'Your Hotel/Restaurant is Closed' Redirect
scams.avoidance: Always walk to your destination and check for yourself This is the #1 most common scam in all of Cuba — nearly every tourist experiences it Trust your map over any stranger's advice about what's open
scams.location: Anywhere in Old Havana and Centro Habana

scams.name: Fake Cohiba Cigars
scams.avoidance: Buy cigars only from official Casa del Habano shops — the only guarantee of authenticity Genuine Cohiba at half price from a street vendor is simply not possible If you want to experience Cuban tobacco culture honestly, visit a legal outlet

scams.name: Peso MN vs. CUP Confusion
scams.avoidance: Familiarize yourself with Cuban peso bills and their values before arriving Always count change before leaving the counter Bring small denominations yourself so you don't need to make change
scams.location: Markets, small restaurants, and local transport

scams.name: Overpriced 'Local' Casa Particular
scams.avoidance: Book casa particulares in advance through Airbnb or Cuba-specific booking sites Verify your accommodation address independently before following anyone to it Licensed casas have a blue door sign — check for it

scams.name: Fake Rum & Mojito Bait-and-Switch
scams.avoidance: Ask for the bottle to be poured in front of you from a sealed or visibly full bottle Stick to established bars with good reputations rather than random tourist-strip spots Buy bottles from a state liquor store (tienda) if you want to guarantee authenticity
scams.location: Bars and restaurants in tourist zones
